name: The Lodge at Torrey Pines
positioning: Craftsman-style resort with a full-service spa, set directly next to Torrey Pines Golf Course with views of the Pacific Ocean
best_for: Golfers who want to stay right next to Torrey Pines Golf Course
Families looking for a kids program and outdoor space near hiking trails

facts.text: The Lodge overlooks Torrey Pines Golf Course, with views of the Pacific Ocean.
The resort is designed in a Craftsman style.
The Lodge reopened in 2002 as an homage to the early California Craftsman architecture of the early 1900s.
Guests pulling into the circular driveway are greeted by doormen in traditional Scottish kilts.
The lobby features amber-hued stained glass, hand-carved woodwork and Arts and Crafts style lanterns.
Besides the spa pool, there is a separate oversized swimming pool.
The property has a croquet lawn.
A.R. Valentien's seasonal menu emphasizes farm-to-table sourcing and produce from Southern California growers.
The Grill is the Lodge's casual, open-air patio restaurant.
There are ADA-compliant rooms across the property, from Signature Rooms to Palisade Suites.

highlights.text: The Palisade Suites have private patios with views over Torrey Pines Golf Course and the Pacific Ocean in the distance.
The Lodge sits directly next to Torrey Pines Golf Course, and guests who book a package through the hotel are guaranteed a tee time on the North Course.
The Lodge is within walking distance of Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve, which has miles of hiking trails.
The full-service spa has a dedicated steam and sauna area and a heated outdoor pool framed by cabanas and loungers.
The Learn at The Lodge program for kids comes in four- and eight-hour options.

considerations.text: The hotel sits between La Jolla to the south and Del Mar to the north; outside the golf course and the reserve, there is not much within easy walking distance.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.
WhataHotel notes limited on-site entertainment options.
